bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42521166 (hdf5): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target h5_extended_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42521166
bug_description.normalized: The superblock extension object header can contain a later zero-sized FSINFO message after an earlier valid version-0 FSINFO message. `H5F__super_read` decodes the first FSINFO, sees `fsinfo.mapped = TRUE`, and in read/write mode removes all FSINFO messages. During that removal, `H5O__msg_iterate_real` lazily decodes the later zero-sized FSINFO. In `H5O__fsinfo_decode`, the version-byte bounds check uses an off-by-one end-pointer model (`p_end = p + p_size` with `if (p + 1 - 1 > p_end)`), so the empty-body case is not rejected before `vers = *p++`, causing a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: Attacker-controlled superblock-extension object-header bytes are materialized into the heap-backed chunk image that later supplies both FSINFO descriptors.
source.value_from: The staged fuzz input bytes are written to disk by `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` and then parsed by HDF5; this memcpy loads the resulting object-header image into `oh->chunk[chunkno].image`.
source.note: The superblock extension object header from the PoC is copied into the heap chunk buffer that ASan later reports as a 75-byte over-read allocation context.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: The FSINFO decoder dereferences the message-body pointer even though the later malformed FSINFO descriptor contributes no valid version byte.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at this line in `H5O__fsinfo_decode`.

root_cause.description: The version-byte guard interprets `p_end` incorrectly and fails to reject the empty-body case before the version dereference.
root_cause.note: With `p_end` derived as `p + p_size`, the `>` comparison treats `p == p_end` as safe. The fix changes both the end sentinel and the check (`H5_IS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW(p, 1, p_end)`) so zero remaining bytes are rejected.

tainted_value_origin.note: The fuzzer buffer is written verbatim to a temporary HDF5 file, which `H5Fopen` then parses.

fine_trace.note: The superblock-extension object-header image from the attacker-controlled HDF5 file is copied into the heap-backed chunk buffer that later becomes the over-read allocation.
When the parser reaches the later message header in the same extension object header, the staged PoC bytes at offset `0x68` decode to `id = 0x0017` (`FSINFO`) and `mesg_size = 0`.
The chunk-boundary check only rejects bodies whose declared size extends past `eom_ptr`. Because this later FSINFO header declares `mesg_size = 0`, the malformed message is accepted as in-bounds.
The later FSINFO descriptor records the start of its body in `mesg->raw` and stores `mesg->raw_size = 0`, so any later decode of that descriptor receives an empty message body.

A different FSINFO message earlier in the same extension object header has a 32-byte body whose first byte is `0x00`, so when `H5F__super_read` decodes that first FSINFO it takes the version-0 path and sets `fsinfo.mapped = TRUE`.

Because the first FSINFO decoded as mapped and the harness opened the file with `H5F_ACC_RDWR`, `H5F__super_read` takes the rewrite path that removes all FSINFO messages from the superblock extension.

`H5F__super_ext_remove_msg` calls `H5O_msg_remove(&ext_loc, H5O_FSINFO_ID, H5O_ALL, TRUE)`, so removal iterates every FSINFO descriptor, not just the first one already read. When iteration reaches the later malformed FSINFO, this macro passes `idx_msg->raw` and `idx_msg->raw_size` (`0`) into `H5O__fsinfo_decode`.
For the later malformed descriptor, `p_size` is `0`, so `p_end` is set equal to `p` rather than to a last valid byte in the message body.

This guard compares against the exclusive-end pointer from the previous step using `>`. With `p == p_end`, the condition is false, so the decoder does not reject the case where no version byte is available.
The decoder reads one byte for the FSINFO version even though the later descriptor contributed no valid body bytes. ASan reports the resulting 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at this line.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is an HDF5 file whose v2 superblock points to a superblock extension object header at `0x30`. Static parsing of that extension shows one FSINFO message at `0x40` with encoded size `0x20` and first body byte `0x00` (so `H5O__fsinfo_decode` marks it mapped), followed later by another FSINFO header at `0x68` whose encoded body size is `0`. When the harness opens the file with `H5Fopen(filename, H5F_ACC_RDWR, ...)`, `H5F__super_read` removes all FSINFO messages and lazily decodes the later zero-sized FSINFO, reaching the off-by-one version-byte check and the 1-byte out-of-bounds read.

format.name: hdf5-superblock-extension-fsinfo
format.contract: An HDF5 file with a v2 superblock whose superblock-extension object header contains at least two FSINFO message headers in the same chunk: an earlier version-0 FSINFO that decodes as mapped, and a later FSINFO whose encoded body size is exactly `0`. The file must be opened with write intent so `H5F__super_read` removes all FSINFO messages and decodes the later zero-sized descriptor during removal.
